newsitem.title: USA: Report of possible Pepsi spin-off sends stock soaring.
newsitem.headline: Report of possible Pepsi spin-off sends stock soaring.

text.p: A published report that PepsiCo Inc. could announce the spin-off of its $11 billion restaurant business as early as Thursday set off frantic action in the company's stock, sending it 10 percent higher.
By midday Thursday, Pepsi stock traded up $3.125 at $35. More than 17 million shares traded, topping the New York Stock Exchange's top 10 actives list.
A report in The Wall Street Journal said the company's board was scheduled to meet on Thursday. The company later confirmed that a meeting was scheduled.
There has been speculation that Pepsi would spin off its $11 billion restaurant division, which includes Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Kentucky Fried Chicken.
A spin-off of the three chains would create one of the largest fast-food companies in the world.
The Journal said it is unclear if the company's international operations, which account for about 18 percent of its restaurant sales, would be included in a spin-off.
Any separation of Pepsico's restaurant operations from its core beverage and Frito-Lay snack business will improve the company's credit quality, according to Fitch Investor Services.
Pepsico's restaurant segment has underperformed its peers in the fast-food industry, Fitch said.
A spin-off would allow Chief Financial Officer Karl Von der Heyden and Chief Executive Officer Roger Enrico to concentrate on building Pepsico's soft drink and snack units, Fitch said in a report.
